docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• never commit .env
  • preserve SCIPION_HOME during normal upgrades
  • use strong secrets
  • read the actual persisted API_PORT instead of assuming a port
  • keep API/Web releases aligned in normal deployments
  • use HTTPS/reverse proxying for public production exposure
  • back up PostgreSQL and important configuration before risky maintenance
  • prefer managed install/update/uninstall commands over manual filesystem deletion

docs.title: Common configuration smells
docs.text:
Watch for:

  • .env values pointing to an old installation path
  • a frontend deployed correctly but using the wrong API base path
  • a service started under a different SCIPION_HOME
  • operational scripts assuming port 8080 while the installation selected another port
  • stale WEB_DIST_PATH after manual file moves
  • inconsistent PostgreSQL values between DATABASE_URL and split settings

When behavior looks inconsistent, inspect the resolved runtime paths and .env before assuming a code defect.

docs.title: Environment Variables (.env)
docs.text:
SCIPION_HOME/.env is the central persistent runtime configuration for ScipionAPI.

Typical location:

<SCIPION_HOME>/.env

For a standard guided installation:

<installation-root>/scipion_home/.env

The file stores runtime/service/database configuration that must survive managed application-code updates.

Sensitive configuration

.env can contain database credentials, secret keys, and service endpoints. Do not commit it to source control and protect its filesystem permissions.

docs.title: What is configured here
docs.text:
Common configuration groups include:

  • PostgreSQL connection/bootstrap values
  • application secret key
  • API host and selected port
  • Redis/Celery settings
  • logs/projects/runtime paths
  • integrated Web deployment settings
  • Conda executable/activation metadata
  • update metadata

The exact set evolves with ScipionAPI versions. Treat the installed CLI/code as authoritative for supported keys.

docs.title: Database settings
docs.text:
Typical values include:

DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@host:5432/database
DATABASE_NAME=scipion_db
DATABASE_USER=scipion_user
DATABASE_PASS=<database-password>

Keep the split database values consistent with DATABASE_URL when both are present. Inconsistent values can make bootstrap, administration, and runtime connectivity behave differently.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
A strong application secret is required:

SECRET_KEY=<strong-random-secret>

Use a long private value and protect the .env file from unauthorized reading.

docs.title: API runtime
docs.text:
Typical runtime keys include:

API_HOST=0.0.0.0
API_PORT=<selected-port>

docs.title: Automatic port selection
docs.text:
Do not assume that new installations always use port 8080.

When install/provision is called without --api-port:

  1. an existing configured API_PORT is preserved when appropriate
  2. otherwise a free port is selected automatically
  3. that value is persisted in .env

Read the actual value:

grep '^API_PORT=' "$SCIPION_HOME/.env"

If a fixed port is operationally required, pass --api-port PORT during installation/provisioning.

Reverse proxy deployments

The selected API port can remain an internal service port behind nginx/Apache or another reverse proxy. Public HTTPS exposure does not require hardcoding a particular backend port in the release bundle.

docs.title: Redis / Celery
docs.text:
Typical broker configuration:

BROKER_URL=redis://localhost:6379/0
CELERY_LOGLEVEL=info

Redis must remain reachable for Celery background processing.

docs.title: Runtime filesystem paths
docs.text:
Examples:

LOGS_PATH=/path/to/scipion_home/logs
PROJECTS_PATH=/path/to/scipion_home/projects

Depending on the installation version, paths may be absolute or resolved from the runtime workspace. Ensure the service user owns/has write access to the required runtime directories.

docs.title: Integrated Web mode
docs.text:
Integrated deployments commonly include:

SERVE_WEB=1
API_MOUNT_PATH=/api
WEB_DIST_PATH=/path/to/scipion_home/web/dist
WEB_API_BASE_URL=/api

Roles:

  • SERVE_WEB=1 enables frontend serving from ScipionAPI
  • API_MOUNT_PATH controls where the REST API is mounted
  • WEB_DIST_PATH identifies the deployed compiled frontend
  • WEB_API_BASE_URL tells the Web UI which API base path/URL to use

For the normal integrated configuration, API_MOUNT_PATH and WEB_API_BASE_URL are usually both /api.

docs.title: Conda integration
docs.text:
Provisioning can persist Conda information such as:

CONDA_EXE=/home/user/miniconda3/bin/conda
CONDA_ACTIVATION_CMD=...

These values depend on the real Conda installation and should generally be managed by the provisioning/bootstrap flow rather than guessed manually.

docs.title: Administrator bootstrap metadata
docs.text:
The installation flow can persist non-secret administrator identity metadata when useful, for example username/email depending on release behavior.

Administrator passwords should be supplied through hidden prompts or temporary environment variables such as those used by the installer/CLI.

Do not rely on plaintext admin passwords in .env

The normal password flow uses the password to create/update the account. Do not add ADMIN_PASSWORD=<real-password> to .env as an operational shortcut.

docs.title: Update metadata
docs.text:
Successful updates can record metadata such as:

SCIPIONAPI_LAST_UPDATE_VERSION=v4.0.1
SCIPIONAPI_LAST_UPDATE_AT=20260812T143000Z
SCIPIONAPI_UPDATE_BASE_URL=https://scipion.cnb.csic.es/downloads/scipion/scipionWeb/

This helps the backend/UI describe installed release state and update availability.

docs.title: Example integrated .env
docs.text:
The exact generated values depend on the installation, but conceptually:

DATABASE_URL=postgresql://scipion_user:<database-password>@localhost:5432/scipion_db
DATABASE_NAME=scipion_db
DATABASE_USER=scipion_user
DATABASE_PASS=<database-password>

SECRET_KEY=<strong-random-secret>

API_HOST=0.0.0.0
API_PORT=39080

BROKER_URL=redis://localhost:6379/0
CELERY_LOGLEVEL=info

LOGS_PATH=/home/user/scipionweb/scipion_home/logs
PROJECTS_PATH=/home/user/scipionweb/scipion_home/projects

SERVE_WEB=1
API_MOUNT_PATH=/api
WEB_DIST_PATH=/home/user/scipionweb/scipion_home/web/dist
WEB_API_BASE_URL=/api

39080 is only an example. Read the real API_PORT generated for your installation.

docs.title: Loading .env in a shell
docs.text:
When an administrative workflow genuinely needs the variables exported into the current shell:

set -a
source "$SCIPION_HOME/.env"
set +a

Be careful when doing this in shared shells because secrets become environment variables for child processes.

docs.title: Back up configuration
docs.text:
Before significant manual configuration or database changes:

cp "$SCIPION_HOME/.env" "$SCIPION_HOME/.env.backup"

For normal managed upgrades, the updater is designed to preserve the runtime workspace/configuration, but keeping an administrative backup remains sensible for important systems.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
A common restrictive configuration is:

chmod 600 "$SCIPION_HOME/.env"

Ensure ownership matches the account that operates ScipionWeb.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
Assuming port 8080

Resolve API_PORT from .env or runtime output. Automatic port selection is intentional.

Stale WEB_DIST_PATH

If Web assets are moved manually, integrated mode can point to old content. Normal update/deployment commands should manage the Web distribution path for you.

Mismatched API paths

In integrated mode, keep API_MOUNT_PATH and WEB_API_BASE_URL aligned unless a custom topology requires otherwise.

Database values disagree

Avoid inconsistent DATABASE_URL, database name, user, or password settings.

Editing generated Conda settings casually

Test status, doctor, and restart after any manual change to Conda/runtime configuration.

docs.title: Quick verification
docs.text:
test -f "$SCIPION_HOME/.env" && echo ".env found"
grep -E '^(DATABASE_URL|API_HOST|API_PORT|BROKER_URL|SERVE_WEB|API_MOUNT_PATH|WEB_DIST_PATH)=' \
  "$SCIPION_HOME/.env" || true

Then verify the runtime using the persisted port:

API_PORT="$(grep '^API_PORT=' "$SCIPION_HOME/.env" | tail -n 1 | cut -d= -f2-)"
curl "http://localhost:${API_PORT}/health"

Finally:

./scripts/scipionapi status
./scripts/scipionapi doctor --quick

docs.title: API + Web Integrated Mode
docs.text:
Integrated mode allows ScipionAPI to serve the compiled ScipionWeb frontend and REST API from one runtime endpoint.

This is the normal user-facing mode selected by the guided installer.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
In the standard integrated configuration:

  • Web UI is served at /
  • API is mounted under /api
  • API docs are available under /api/docs

The host port is runtime configuration, not a fixed release property.

Read the actual port from the installed environment:

grep '^API_PORT=' "$SCIPION_HOME/.env"

Then the normal URLs are:

http://localhost:<API_PORT>/
http://localhost:<API_PORT>/api/docs

Automatic port selection

When no fixed --api-port is supplied, provisioning can select a free port automatically and persist it in .env.

docs.title: Recommended installation path
docs.text:
For a new integrated installation:

wget https://scipion.cnb.csic.es/downloads/scipion/scipionWeb/install.sh
chmod +x install.sh
./install.sh --check-only
./install.sh

The installer resolves a paired API + Web release, verifies checksums, and delegates integrated runtime setup to provision.

docs.title: Direct/manual integrated provision
docs.text:
Advanced users can deploy a specific compiled Web artifact directly:

./scripts/scipionapi provision \
  --user "admin" \
  --email "admin@example.org" \
  --web-dist /path/to/ScipionWeb-vX.Y.Z-dist.zip

During provisioning, ScipionAPI deploys the Web assets under the runtime workspace and configures the frontend/API relationship.

docs.title: Runtime behavior
docs.text:
With integrated mode enabled:

/             → compiled ScipionWeb frontend
/api/...      → REST API
/api/docs     → OpenAPI/Swagger documentation

Example using the real configured port:

API_PORT="$(grep '^API_PORT=' "$SCIPION_HOME/.env" | tail -n 1 | cut -d= -f2-)"

curl "http://localhost:${API_PORT}/health"

Open:

http://localhost:<API_PORT>/
http://localhost:<API_PORT>/api/docs

docs.title: Important .env settings
docs.text:
A typical integrated installation includes:

SERVE_WEB=1
API_MOUNT_PATH=/api
WEB_DIST_PATH=/path/to/scipion_home/web/dist
WEB_API_BASE_URL=/api
API_PORT=<selected-port>

Roles:

  • SERVE_WEB=1 enables frontend serving
  • API_MOUNT_PATH controls where the REST API is mounted
  • WEB_DIST_PATH identifies the deployed frontend files
  • WEB_API_BASE_URL tells the frontend where to call the API
  • API_PORT is the persisted listening port

In the normal configuration, API_MOUNT_PATH and WEB_API_BASE_URL are both /api.

docs.title: Runtime frontend configuration
docs.text:
The compiled Web build is designed to be reusable across installations.

ScipionAPI injects/deploys runtime API configuration so the same Web release does not need to be rebuilt for every host or selected port.

This means:

  • release ZIPs remain installation-independent
  • automatic port selection does not require rebuilding ScipionWeb
  • reverse proxies can be introduced without publishing a new frontend artifact

docs.title: When integrated mode is a good fit
docs.text:
Use it for:

  • normal guided installations
  • single-host deployments
  • local/on-prem installations
  • internal lab servers
  • deployments where operational simplicity matters

Advantages include:

  • same-origin API/UI traffic
  • simple networking
  • no separate static Web host requirement
  • one update path for paired API + Web releases

docs.title: When to use a separate deployment
docs.text:
A separate frontend/backend topology may be appropriate when:

  • Web assets are served by a CDN/static host
  • API and frontend scale independently
  • network/security zones require separation
  • an existing infrastructure already provides static frontend hosting

See Separate Deployment.

docs.title: 1. Runtime status
docs.text:
./scripts/scipionapi status
./scripts/scipionapi doctor --quick

docs.title: 2. Resolve the actual port
docs.text:
API_PORT="$(grep '^API_PORT=' "$SCIPION_HOME/.env" | tail -n 1 | cut -d= -f2-)"
echo "$API_PORT"

docs.title: 3. Health endpoint
docs.text: curl "http://localhost:${API_PORT}/health"

docs.title: 4. Browser
docs.text:
Open:

http://localhost:<API_PORT>/
http://localhost:<API_PORT>/api/docs

docs.title: 5. Browser network requests
docs.text: Confirm API requests use the expected /api/... base path.

docs.title: Common issues
docs.text:
Frontend loads but API calls fail

Check API_MOUNT_PATH, WEB_API_BASE_URL, and any reverse-proxy path rewriting.

Using the wrong port

Read API_PORT from .env; do not assume 8080 unless you explicitly configured it.

Stale Web assets

Use the managed update/deployment workflow so WEB_DIST_PATH points to the intended deployed release.

Opening /docs instead of /api/docs

In the standard integrated configuration, API documentation is under the API mount path.

docs.title: Updating integrated mode
docs.text:
For an installed system:

./scripts/scipionapi update --dry-run
./scripts/scipionapi update

The updater resolves the paired release from manifest.json, verifies checksums, updates managed API files, and redeploys the Web bundle while preserving SCIPION_HOME.

docs.title: SCIPION_HOME and Runtime Layout
docs.text:
SCIPION_HOME is the runtime workspace directory used by ScipionAPI.

It stores runtime configuration, logs, project data, and (in integrated mode) deployed Web assets. This directory is part of your operational state and must not be committed to version control.

Why SCIPION_HOME exists

SCIPION_HOME keeps runtime data separate from the API source/bundle directory, which makes upgrades safer and helps preserve data across version changes.

docs.title: Default Location
docs.text:
If SCIPION_HOME is not set explicitly, ScipionAPI typically uses:

SCIPION_HOME=<repoRoot>/scipion_home

You can override it by exporting the variable before starting the application:

export SCIPION_HOME=/opt/scipionweb/runtime

Production recommendation

In production, use a dedicated path outside the API bundle directory (for example /opt/scipionweb/runtime) so upgrades do not affect runtime data.

docs.title: Typical Directory Structure
docs.text:
Example layout:

scipion_home/
├── .env
├── logs/
│   ├── app.log
│   └── celery.log
├── projects/
│   └── <project folders>
├── config/
└── web/
    └── dist/

Mode-dependent directories

The web/ directory is typically present only in integrated mode (when the API serves the Web UI).

docs.title: What Each Path Is Used For
.env
docs.text:
Primary runtime configuration file.

It typically contains:

  • Database connection settings
  • Security-related values (for example SECRET_KEY)
  • Runtime paths
  • Deployment mode flags
  • API and broker configuration

Sensitive file

The .env file may contain credentials and secrets. Protect file permissions and never commit it to version control.

docs.title: logs/
docs.text:
Stores runtime logs, commonly including:

  • API logs
  • Celery worker logs

Typical uses:

  • Debugging errors
  • Operational monitoring
  • Post-incident inspection

Log rotation

In production, plan a log rotation strategy (system-managed logs, logrotate, or journald-based logging depending on your deployment approach).

docs.title: projects/
docs.text:
Stores project runtime data, such as:

  • Scipion projects
  • Generated previews
  • Runtime artifacts

This directory can grow significantly over time depending on project size and usage patterns.

Disk usage growth

Monitor available disk space and define a backup/retention strategy, especially for production or shared environments.

docs.title: config/
docs.text:
Optional location for Scipion-related runtime configuration files and generated configuration state, depending on your deployment and tooling.

Contents may vary

The exact contents of config/ may differ across versions or deployment workflows.

docs.title: web/
docs.text:
Present when using integrated mode.

Typical contents:

web/dist/
    index.html
    assets/
    config.js

This directory stores the deployed frontend assets served by the API.

Web bundle upgrades

When upgrading the integrated Web UI, the deployed contents under web/ may be replaced by a new --web-dist deployment.

docs.title: Permissions and Ownership
docs.text:
Ensure that the service user (or the user running ScipionAPI) has the correct access to SCIPION_HOME.

Minimum recommendations:

  • Read/write access to SCIPION_HOME
  • Write access to logs/, projects/, and deployed runtime paths
  • Read access to .env
  • Enough free disk space for project growth and logs

Permission mismatches

Avoid mixing root-owned files with services running as a non-root user. This is a common cause of startup failures and runtime write errors.

docs.title: Backup Strategy
docs.text:
A practical backup strategy should include:

  • PostgreSQL database backup
  • Entire scipion_home/projects/ directory
  • SCIPION_HOME/.env
  • Any deployment-specific runtime configuration you rely on

Upgrade safety

Before upgrading ScipionAPI/ScipionWeb, back up both the database and key SCIPION_HOME contents so you can recover configuration and project data if needed.

docs.title: Production Recommendations
docs.text:
For production deployments, prefer a dedicated runtime path such as:

/opt/scipionweb/runtime

instead of storing runtime data inside the API source or extracted bundle directory.

Recommended practices:

  • Keep SCIPION_HOME outside version-controlled directories
  • Protect .env permissions
  • Monitor disk usage in projects/ and logs/
  • Back up runtime data regularly
  • Reuse the same SCIPION_HOME across API bundle upgrades (when appropriate)

docs.title: Common Mistakes
docs.text:
Using a temporary directory

Do not place SCIPION_HOME under /tmp or other ephemeral locations. You may lose logs, configuration, and project data.

Forgetting to export SCIPION_HOME after upgrade

If you move to a new API bundle directory and forget to export the existing SCIPION_HOME, the application may create a new empty runtime workspace and appear misconfigured.

Committing runtime files

Avoid committing scipion_home/ or .env files into Git repositories.

docs.title: Quick Verification
docs.text:
Run these checks to confirm the runtime workspace is correctly configured:

echo "$SCIPION_HOME"
ls -al "$SCIPION_HOME"
test -f "$SCIPION_HOME/.env" && echo ".env found"
test -d "$SCIPION_HOME/projects" && echo "projects/ found"
test -d "$SCIPION_HOME/logs" && echo "logs/ found"

If a path is missing

Some directories may be created lazily depending on how the application is used. The most critical item to verify early is SCIPION_HOME/.env.

← Previous: Configuration Overview Next: Environment Variables (.env) →

docs.title: Separate Deployment (API and Web on Different Hosts)
docs.text:
In a separate deployment, the API backend and the Web frontend are deployed independently.

Typical architecture:

  • API runs on one server (or service)
  • Web frontend runs on another host, static server, or CDN

Production-friendly pattern

This deployment model is common in production environments because it enables independent scaling, frontend hosting optimization, and clearer separation of responsibilities.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
A simplified request flow looks like this:

User Browser → Web Server / CDN → REST API → PostgreSQL / Redis

In practice:

  • The browser loads the frontend from a web host (or CDN)
  • The frontend sends API requests to the ScipionAPI host
  • The API talks to PostgreSQL and Redis

docs.title: When to Use Separate Deployment
docs.text:
This mode is recommended for:

  • Production environments
  • Cloud deployments
  • Enterprise setups
  • Load-balanced infrastructure
  • CDN/static hosting for the frontend
  • Teams that deploy frontend and backend independently

Best for scale and flexibility

If you need independent release cycles or web performance optimization, separate deployment is usually the better choice.

docs.title: Frontend Configuration
docs.text: The frontend must know the public base URL of the API.

docs.title: Frontend .env (example)
docs.text: VITE_API_URL="https://api.yourdomain.com"

docs.title: Frontend config usage example
docs.text:
export const BASE_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL;

After changing frontend environment variables, rebuild (or redeploy) the frontend.

Rebuild required

For most Vite-based frontends, environment variables are injected at build time. Changing VITE_API_URL usually requires a rebuild.

docs.title: API Configuration
docs.text: In separate deployment mode, the API should not serve the frontend.

docs.title: Disable integrated mode
docs.text: SERVE_WEB=0

docs.title: CORS configuration
docs.text:
The API must allow the frontend origin(s). Example backend configuration:

allow_origins=["http://web-host:5173"]

Production example:

allow_origins=["https://yourdomain.com"]

CORS is required

If CORS is not configured correctly, browser requests may fail even when the API is healthy and reachable.

docs.title: API server
docs.text: https://api.yourdomain.com

docs.title: Web server (frontend)
docs.text: https://yourdomain.com

docs.title: Example API request from the frontend
docs.text:
https://api.yourdomain.com/api/projects

Consistent public URLs

Keep the frontend's configured API URL aligned with the actual public API endpoint exposed through your reverse proxy / load balancer.

docs.title: TLS / HTTPS
docs.text:
Use HTTPS on both sides in production:

  • Frontend host (web app)
  • API host (backend)

docs.title: Firewalls / security groups
docs.text:
Allow inbound access only to what is needed:

  • Public web ports (80 / 443) on frontend host
  • Public or controlled access to API host (usually 443 behind a reverse proxy)
  • Internal database/Redis access restricted to trusted hosts/services

docs.title: Reverse proxy alignment
docs.text:
If the API is mounted under /api, ensure your reverse proxy configuration preserves the expected path.

Path rewrite mistakes

Misconfigured reverse proxies can strip or duplicate /api, causing 404s even though the backend is running.

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text:
• Independent scaling of frontend and backend
  • CDN support and static hosting optimization
  • Better frontend performance at scale
  • Clear separation of concerns
  • Independent deployment pipelines

docs.title: Considerations and Tradeoffs
docs.text:
• CORS configuration is required
  • SSL/TLS must be configured correctly
  • More moving parts than integrated mode
  • DNS, proxy, and firewall configuration become part of deployment operations

Operational complexity vs flexibility

Separate deployment adds infrastructure complexity, but it pays off in flexibility and scalability for larger environments.

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text:
• [ ] VITE_API_URL points to the correct public API URL
  • [ ] Frontend rebuilt/redeployed after env changes
  • [ ] HTTPS enabled on the frontend host

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• [ ] SERVE_WEB=0
  • [ ] CORS allows the frontend origin(s)
  • [ ] API mounted and proxied correctly (for example /api)
  • [ ] HTTPS enabled on the public API endpoint

docs.title: Infrastructure
docs.text:
• [ ] DNS resolves frontend and API domains correctly
  • [ ] Firewall/security groups allow required traffic only
  • [ ] Reverse proxy forwards API paths as expected

docs.title: 1. Check API health directly
docs.text:
curl https://api.yourdomain.com/health

(adjust the URL/path to your actual public API endpoint)

docs.title: 2. Test a browser session
docs.text:
• Open the frontend URL
  • Log in (if applicable)
  • Open browser developer tools
  • Confirm API requests go to the expected API domain/path

docs.title: 3. Validate CORS behavior
docs.text: Look for browser console/network errors such as blocked cross-origin requests.

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
CORS error in browser

The frontend origin is missing from the backend CORS allow list (or the scheme/port does not match exactly).

Frontend still calls old API host

VITE_API_URL was changed but the frontend was not rebuilt/redeployed.

API reachable from curl but not from browser

This usually indicates a CORS issue, mixed-content issue (HTTPS page calling HTTP API), or an incorrect frontend API base URL.

404 on /api/... behind reverse proxy

Check proxy path forwarding and backend mount path alignment.

docs.title: Integrated Mode
docs.text:
• Simpler setup
  • Single host / single endpoint
  • No CORS in common deployments
  • Easier for local/internal use

docs.title: Separate Deployment
docs.text:
• More flexible and scalable
  • Frontend and API deploy independently
  • CORS and proxy configuration required
  • Better fit for cloud/production platforms
← Previous: API + Web Integrated Mode

docs.title: Common Errors and Fixes
docs.text:
This page collects frequent development-time problems and the fastest checks to resolve them.

Use this page for local dev issues

If your problem is more related to deployed services, production startup, or runtime operations, also check Backend Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Quick Triage Checklist
docs.text:
Before going deep, verify the basics:

conda activate scipion4Web
./scripts/scipionapi status
curl http://localhost:8080/health
redis-cli ping

Then confirm:

  • you are using the expected Conda environment
  • SCIPION_HOME points to the right runtime workspace
  • .env exists and contains the expected values
  • PostgreSQL and Redis are reachable
  • API and Celery are reading the same runtime configuration

docs.title: Typical cause
docs.text: You are not running inside the expected Conda environment, or the worker was started outside the environment prepared by the wrapper script.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
conda activate scipion4Web
python -c "import pyworkflow; print(pyworkflow.__file__)"

If you are using the wrapper script, rerun the command from the ScipionAPI bundle directory:

./scripts/scipionapi restart

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text: KeyError: DATABASE_URL

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
• Ensure SCIPION_HOME/.env exists
  • Ensure SCIPION_HOME is exported correctly
  • Restart the API after changing environment values

Useful check:

echo "$SCIPION_HOME"
test -f "$SCIPION_HOME/.env" && echo ".env found"

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• missing table errors
  • duplicate revision errors
  • multiple heads
  • Can't locate revision identified by ...

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
• inspect migration state with alembic heads and alembic current
  • verify you are targeting the correct database
  • avoid editing migrations that were already applied
  • test on a fresh empty database when state is unclear

For real deployments, create a database backup before stamping or repairing migration state.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
sudo systemctl start redis-server
sudo systemctl status redis-server
redis-cli ping

Expected output:

PONG

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
• the worker is running
  • Redis is reachable
  • the broker URL matches between API and worker
  • worker logs show task receipt/execution
  • SCIPION_HOME is available to the worker process

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
./scripts/scipionapi status
./scripts/scipionapi logs
redis-cli ping

If tasks stay in PENDING, confirm both the API and the worker are using the same runtime configuration.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• requests work with curl but fail in the browser
  • preflight or origin errors appear in DevTools

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
• add the exact frontend origin to the backend CORS configuration
  • verify scheme, host, and port match the real frontend URL
  • check that reverse proxies are not rewriting origins unexpectedly

For local development, the browser origin is usually similar to:

http://localhost:5173

The API may be running at:

http://localhost:8080

Both values must match the configured development setup.

docs.title: 7. JWT invalid signature or invalid token
Typical causes
docs.text:
• SECRET_KEY mismatch
  • expired token
  • stale token stored in the browser

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
• ensure the API is using the expected SECRET_KEY
  • clear stored tokens or log in again
  • restart the backend if configuration changed recently

A private browser window is a quick way to test whether stale local state is involved.

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text: Address already in use

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
Identify the process first:

lsof -i :8080

Then stop it only if it is safe to do so:

kill <pid>

Use forceful termination only as a last resort:

kill -9 <pid>

Or change the configured API port if another service is meant to keep using that port.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
chmod -R u+rwX "$SCIPION_HOME"

Also confirm that the same user owns the runtime files and starts the services:

ls -ld "$SCIPION_HOME"
ls -ld "$SCIPION_HOME/logs"

docs.title: 10. When to escalate to backend troubleshooting
docs.text:
Go to Backend Troubleshooting when the issue involves:

  • deployed services that do not start correctly
  • database connectivity in shared or production environments
  • Redis or Celery runtime mismatches
  • authentication problems that reproduce outside local development

For recurring operational problems, also check Known Issues and Workarounds.

docs.title: Suggested Debugging Order
docs.text:
1. Check the active Conda environment
  2. Validate SCIPION_HOME and .env
  3. Test PostgreSQL and Redis reachability
  4. Review API and Celery logs
  5. Restart services and retry the failing workflow

docs.title: Local Development Workflow
docs.text:
This guide describes the recommended workflow for developing ScipionAPI locally.

It assumes:

  • Linux environment
  • Conda installed
  • PostgreSQL and Redis running locally

docs.title: 1. Clone Repository
docs.text:
git clone <repository-url>
cd ScipionAPI

docs.title: 2. Bootstrap Environment
docs.text:
./scripts/scipionapi bootstrap

Activate environment:

conda activate scipion4Web

docs.title: 3. Configure Runtime Workspace
docs.text:
Create a development runtime directory:

export SCIPION_HOME=$(pwd)/scipion_home
mkdir -p "$SCIPION_HOME"

Run install:

./scripts/scipionapi install \
  --user admin \
  --email admin@example.org

docs.title: 4. Start Development Server
docs.text:
Instead of using start, run uvicorn manually:

uvicorn app.backend.main:app --reload --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080

This enables auto-reload on code changes.

docs.title: 5. Start Celery Worker
docs.text:
In another terminal:

celery -A app.workers.task_queue worker --loglevel=info

docs.title: 6. Verify
docs.text:
Open:

http://localhost:8080/docs

docs.title: Recommended Workflow
docs.text:
During development:

  • Use manual uvicorn with --reload
  • Do not use detached start
  • Keep logs visible in terminal
  • Use separate database for development

docs.title: Frontend Local Development
docs.text:
If developing frontend:

npm run dev

Ensure:

VITE_API_URL="http://localhost:8080"

docs.title: Suggested Branch Strategy
docs.text:
• main → stable
  • devel → active development
  • feature/* → feature branches

docs.title: Current Celery Development Topology
docs.text: The current ScipionAPI runtime routes background work through two dedicated queues. When developing or debugging routed tasks manually, use two Celery terminals rather than relying on a single generic worker.

docs.title: Terminal 1: FastAPI
docs.text: uvicorn app.backend.main:app --reload --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080

docs.title: Terminal 2: Plugin worker
docs.text: python -m celery -A app.workers.task_queue worker --loglevel info --hostname plugins@%h -Q plugins --concurrency 1 --prefetch-multiplier 1

docs.title: Terminal 3: Protocol worker
docs.text:
python -m celery -A app.workers.task_queue worker --loglevel info --hostname protocols@%h -Q protocols --concurrency 4 --prefetch-multiplier 1

The plugin worker deliberately runs with concurrency 1. Protocol-worker concurrency defaults to 4 and can be adjusted through PROTOCOL_WORKER_CONCURRENCY when the runtime is started through the ScipionAPI CLI.

Verify worker connectivity with:

python -m celery -A app.workers.task_queue inspect ping

This split setup mirrors the current ./scripts/scipionapi start worker topology while keeping all processes visible in separate development terminals.

docs.title: Debugging with PyCharm
docs.text: This guide explains how to configure PyCharm for backend debugging.

docs.title: 1. Open Project
docs.text: Open the ScipionAPI directory in PyCharm.

docs.title: 2. Configure Python Interpreter
docs.text:
Go to:

Settings → Project → Python Interpreter

Select:

Conda environment → scipion4Web

If not detected, manually point to:

~/miniconda3/envs/scipion4Web/bin/python

docs.title: 3. Create Run Configuration
docs.text:
Create a new Python configuration:

  • Script path: leave empty
  • Module name:
uvicorn

Parameters:

app.backend.main:app --reload --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080

Working directory:

<project-root>

Environment variables:

SCIPION_HOME=/absolute/path/to/scipion_home

docs.title: 4. Enable Debugging
docs.text:
Set breakpoints inside:

  • routers
  • services
  • models
  • auth dependencies

Run in Debug mode.

docs.title: 5. Debug Celery Tasks
docs.text:
For Celery debugging:

Instead of running separate worker, temporarily call task synchronously in code.

Or configure Celery to run in eager mode (development only).

docs.title: Common Debug Tips
docs.text:
• Ensure correct Conda interpreter selected
  • Ensure SCIPION_HOME is set
  • Verify .env is loaded
  • Use PyCharm database tool to inspect PostgreSQL

docs.title: Recommended PyCharm Settings
docs.text:
• Enable "Reload changed modules"
  • Enable "Show console"
  • Disable aggressive auto-import if interfering

docs.title: Running Uvicorn Manually
docs.text: For development, it is recommended to run Uvicorn manually instead of using the CLI start command.

docs.title: Basic Command
docs.text: uvicorn app.backend.main:app --reload --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080

docs.title: Why Use --reload?
docs.text:
• Automatically reloads on file changes
  • Faster development cycle
  • No need to restart manually

docs.title: Required Environment
docs.text:
Before running:

conda activate scipion4Web
export SCIPION_HOME=$(pwd)/scipion_home

Ensure .env exists inside SCIPION_HOME.

docs.title: Running on Different Port
docs.text: uvicorn app.backend.main:app --reload --port 9000

docs.title: Production Warning
docs.text:
Do NOT use:

--reload

In production.

Production should use:

  • systemd
  • gunicorn + uvicorn workers
  • reverse proxy

docs.title: Example Production Command
docs.text: uvicorn app.backend.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
If import errors appear:

  • Verify correct Conda environment
  • Verify PYTHONPATH includes project root
  • Verify SCIPION_HOME is set

docs.title: Frontend Overview
docs.text:
ScipionWeb is the React-based frontend that provides the graphical user interface for ScipionAPI.

It is built with a modern web stack and distributed as a compiled static bundle that can be deployed in multiple modes.

Scope of this section

This section covers the frontend application model, build pipeline, runtime API URL configuration, and deployment options. Backend internals are documented in the Backend section.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
The frontend is responsible for:

  • User authentication (login/logout)
  • Project browsing
  • Protocol management
  • Output visualization
  • Plugin interaction
  • UI rendering and routing

Backend boundary

Business logic, persistence, and task execution are handled by the backend API. The frontend acts as a client application consuming REST endpoints.

docs.title: Technology Stack
docs.text:
• UI Framework React + TypeScript

Component-based UI with typed application code.

  • Build Tooling Vite

Fast local development server and optimized production builds.

  • API Communication REST over HTTP

The frontend communicates with ScipionAPI using a configurable base URL.

  • Distribution Model Static dist/ bundle

Deployable via API-integrated mode, web servers, or CDN hosting.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
High-level request flow:

Browser → React App → REST API → Backend

The frontend communicates with ScipionAPI through HTTP requests only.

docs.title: Build and Distribution Model
docs.text:
ScipionWeb is typically:

  • Developed in a separate repository
  • Built using Vite
  • Packaged as a static dist/ bundle
  • Served either by:
  • ScipionAPI (integrated mode)
  • A separate web server (separate deployment)
  • CDN/static hosting

docs.title: Runtime API Configuration
docs.text:
The frontend API base URL is controlled by:

VITE_API_URL

Build-time + runtime behavior

The frontend can use VITE_API_URL at build time and may also consume injected runtime configuration in integrated mode.

See: Runtime API URL Configuration

docs.title: Deployment Modes
docs.text:
ScipionWeb supports three main deployment strategies:

  1. Integrated mode (API serves frontend)
  2. Separate deployment (frontend and API on different hosts)
  3. CDN/static hosting (frontend on CDN, API separate)

See: Deployment Options

docs.title: Version Compatibility
docs.text:
The compiled frontend bundle should match a compatible ScipionAPI version.

Recommended practice:

  • Upgrade API and Web together
  • Keep versioned frontend dist bundles
  • Validate API compatibility before production rollout

Common upgrade pitfall

A frontend bundle can load successfully while still failing at runtime if the API version is incompatible (routes, payloads, auth behavior, or config expectations).

docs.title: Recommended Reading Order
docs.text:
1. Build and Dist Output
  2. Runtime API URL Configuration
  3. Deployment Options

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: ← Previous: Backend Overview         Next: Build and Dist Output →

docs.title: Build and Dist Output
docs.text:
ScipionWeb frontend builds are generated with Vite.

This page covers:

  • Local development mode
  • Production builds
  • dist/ output layout
  • Packaging for distribution
  • Integration with ScipionAPI provisioning

docs.title: Development Mode
docs.text:
From inside the frontend repository:

npm install
npm run dev

This starts a local development server (typically):

http://localhost:5173

Frontend-backend pairing

During local development, ensure the backend API is running and reachable from the browser.

docs.title: Development API URL
docs.text:
The frontend API URL should be defined in:

.env

Example:

VITE_API_URL="http://localhost:8080"

Dev env changes require restart

If you change .env, restart the Vite dev server to ensure the new values are applied.

docs.title: Production Build
docs.text:
Generate the production bundle:

npm run build

This creates a static output directory:

dist/
├── index.html
├── assets/
└── ...

docs.title: Dist Output Structure
docs.text:
Example production output:

dist/
├── index.html
├── assets/
│   ├── index-abc123.js
│   ├── index-abc123.css
│   └── ...
└── favicon.ico

The dist/ folder is static and can be:

  • Served by nginx
  • Served by Apache
  • Hosted on a CDN/static platform
  • Mounted into ScipionAPI (integrated mode)

Hashed assets

File names inside assets/ are often content-hashed for cache busting. This is expected behavior in production builds.

docs.title: Packaging for Distribution
docs.text:
To distribute the compiled frontend bundle:

zip -r ScipionWeb-<version>-dist.zip dist/

This ZIP can be used with ScipionAPI provisioning:

./scripts/scipionapi provision --web-dist ScipionWeb-<version>-dist.zip

Versioned artifacts

Keep versioned ZIP files (and optionally build metadata) to simplify rollback and compatibility tracking.

docs.title: Build Verification Checklist
docs.text:
After npm run build, verify:

  • dist/index.html exists
  • dist/assets/ contains JS/CSS bundles
  • The configured API URL strategy matches your deployment mode
  • The bundle version matches the target API version

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
Do not edit dist/ manually

Treat dist/ as generated output. Make source changes in the frontend codebase and rebuild.

Rebuild after config changes

Changes to VITE_API_URL and other build-time env values require a new production build.

Check API compatibility

Ensure the frontend bundle and ScipionAPI version are compatible before production deployment.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: ← Previous: Frontend Overview         Next: Runtime API URL Configuration →

docs.title: Deployment Options
docs.text: ScipionWeb can be deployed in two main ways.

docs.title: Integrated mode
docs.text:
Integrated mode is the recommended option for most installations. In this mode, ScipionAPI serves both the API and the compiled Web UI from the same runtime.

Use this option for local labs, internal installations, and first-time deployments.

docs.title: Separate deployment
docs.text:
In separate deployment mode, the frontend and API are hosted independently.

Use this option only when your infrastructure requires independent frontend and backend hosting.

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text: Use integrated mode unless you have a specific reason to host the frontend separately.

docs.title: Related pages
docs.text:
• Runtime API URL Configuration
  • Integrated Mode
  • Separate Deployment

docs.title: Runtime API URL Configuration
docs.text:
The frontend communicates with ScipionAPI using a base API URL.

This is primarily defined by:

VITE_API_URL

docs.title: Development
docs.text: VITE_API_URL="http://localhost:8080"

docs.title: Production (separate deployment example)
docs.text:
VITE_API_URL="https://api.yourdomain.com"

The variable is typically consumed as:

export const BASE_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL;

Vite behavior

Values from VITE_* variables are injected into the frontend build and are not automatically updated after build time.

docs.title: Integrated Mode (API + Web)
docs.text:
In integrated mode:

  • Web is served at /
  • API is mounted at /api

No external API host is required for the frontend.

The installer can inject runtime configuration through:

window.__SCIPION_WEB_CONFIG__

Example payload:

{
  "apiBaseUrl": "/api"
}

The frontend can prefer this runtime value when present, allowing a single build artifact to adapt to integrated deployments.

Why runtime injection helps

Runtime config avoids rebuilding the frontend just to change the API mount path in integrated scenarios.

docs.title: Separate Deployment
docs.text:
If frontend and API run on different hosts, define the API URL in the frontend .env before building:

VITE_API_URL="https://api.yourdomain.com"

Then rebuild the frontend:

npm run build

docs.title: Configuration Matrix
docs.text: Deployment Mode Frontend Host API Host Typical API Base Integrated Same as API Same as frontend /api Separate https://yourdomain.com https://api.yourdomain.com https://api.yourdomain.com CDN CDN/static host Separate API host https://api.yourdomain.com

docs.title: Common Mistakes
docs.text:
Changing .env without rebuilding

In production builds, VITE_API_URL is compiled into the bundle. Rebuild after changes.

HTTP/HTTPS mismatch

Mixed protocol usage (frontend on HTTPS, API on HTTP) can break requests in browsers.

CORS not configured on backend

Separate deployments require backend CORS configuration for the frontend origin.

Using localhost in production builds

Double-check build artifacts before release to avoid accidentally shipping localhost API URLs.

docs.title: Production Recommendations
docs.text:
• Use HTTPS for frontend and API
  • Use stable domain naming (app. / api. pattern, or integrated /api)
  • Document your API URL strategy per environment (dev/staging/prod)
  • Validate API reachability from the browser before rollout

docs.title: Quick Validation
docs.text:
After deployment, confirm in the browser:

  • Login requests go to the expected API origin/path
  • No CORS errors appear in DevTools
  • No mixed-content warnings appear
  • Network requests return expected responses

docs.title: Installation Overview
docs.text:
Use this section to install ScipionWeb for users, understand the underlying packaged deployment, or upgrade an existing installation.

For a new Linux installation, the recommended path is now the guided install.sh installer. It resolves a matched API + Web release from the public release manifest, downloads the required ZIP files, verifies checksums, and runs the normal ScipionAPI provisioning workflow for you.

Recommended path for most new installations

Follow this sequence:

  1. Prerequisites
  2. Guided Installation

The normal user-facing installation no longer requires manually downloading and pairing the API/Web ZIP files.

docs.title: Fast path
docs.text:
wget https://scipion.cnb.csic.es/downloads/scipion/scipionWeb/install.sh
chmod +x install.sh
./install.sh --check-only
./install.sh

The installer defaults to the release identified as latest in the public manifest.json.

docs.title: Guided installation — recommended
docs.text:
Use Guided Installation when you want:

  • a normal integrated API + Web installation
  • matched API and Web release versions automatically
  • published SHA256 verification
  • automatic port selection when no fixed port is requested
  • a stable installation directory
  • a guided installation marker that enables protected full uninstall later

This is the standard path for new user-facing installations.

docs.title: Manual bundle + provision workflow
docs.text:
Use Download Bundles and Recommended Installation / Provision when you intentionally want to control the downloaded artifacts and run provision yourself.

This remains useful for:

  • deployment debugging
  • custom infrastructure automation
  • API-only scenarios
  • frontend hosted separately
  • advanced testing

docs.title: Manual installation
docs.text:
Use Manual Installation only when you need fine-grained control over each layer, for example:

  • remote PostgreSQL setup
  • unusual database/bootstrap requirements
  • development environments
  • custom deployment topologies
  • troubleshooting low-level installation problems

docs.title: Upgrade an existing installation
docs.text:
Use Upgrade / Reinstall Notes when ScipionWeb is already installed.

The normal updater preserves runtime data and configuration while updating managed API code, the deployed Web bundle, and the managed installer file.

docs.title: What this section covers
docs.text:
The installation documentation includes:

  • system prerequisites such as Conda, PostgreSQL, Redis, ports, and permissions
  • guided installation through the public install.sh
  • manual download and extraction of release bundles
  • one-shot provision for controlled/manual installs
  • low-level manual installation for advanced setups
  • upgrade workflow and rollback guidance
  • production deployment considerations

docs.title: Installation mental model
docs.text:
A useful way to think about installation is:

  1. machine readiness → prerequisites
  2. release resolution → manifest.json
  3. artifacts → matched ScipionAPI + ScipionWeb ZIP files
  4. runtime setup → provision
  5. verification → status, doctor, browser, logs

The guided installer automates steps 2–4 while keeping the same underlying deployment model available to advanced users.

docs.title: Important behavior
docs.text:
API/Web versions stay paired

The guided installer resolves both artifacts from the same release entry. For manual installs, keep ScipionAPI and ScipionWeb versions aligned unless you are intentionally testing compatibility.

The API port is not assumed to be 8080

When no fixed API/Web port is provided, provisioning preserves an existing configured port or selects a free port automatically and persists it in .env.

Existing installation detected

Do not run the new-install path over an existing installation. Use ./scripts/scipionapi update instead.

Backup before important upgrades

The updater protects application files, but database rollback still requires a database backup when schema migrations matter.

docs.title: Production Deployment with systemd
docs.text:
This guide explains how to run ScipionAPI and the Celery worker as systemd services.

Using systemd is recommended for:

  • Production environments
  • Automatic restart on failure
  • Startup on boot
  • Centralized logging with journalctl
  • Stable long-running services

Scope

This page covers a direct systemd deployment (API + Celery worker). If you expose the service to users, a reverse proxy such as nginx is strongly recommended.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A typical production deployment with systemd includes:

  1. Stop CLI-managed services (if running)
  2. Identify installation paths
  3. Create a systemd service for the API
  4. Create a systemd service for the Celery worker
  5. Reload systemd
  6. Enable services on boot
  7. Start services
  8. Verify status and logs

Prerequisite

Make sure the installation is already working (for example via provision) before switching to systemd.

docs.title: 1. Stop CLI-Managed Services
docs.text:
If you previously started services with the ScipionAPI CLI, stop them first to avoid port conflicts and duplicate workers.

./scripts/scipionapi stop

Avoid mixed process management

Do not run the same API/worker both through the CLI and systemd at the same time.

docs.title: 2. Locate Installation Paths
docs.text: Identify the paths used by your deployment.

docs.title: Example API installation directory
docs.text: /opt/scipionweb/ScipionAPI-1.0.0

docs.title: Example SCIPION_HOME
docs.text: /opt/scipionweb/scipion_home

docs.title: Example Conda environment
docs.text:
/home/youruser/miniconda3/envs/scipion4Web

Use absolute paths only

Always use absolute paths in systemd service files (WorkingDirectory, ExecStart, SCIPION_HOME, etc.).

docs.title: 3. Create the systemd Service for the API
docs.text:
Create the service file:

/etc/systemd/system/scipionapi.service

docs.title: Example scipionapi.service
docs.text:
[Unit]
Description=ScipionAPI Service
After=network.target postgresql.service redis-server.service
Wants=postgresql.service redis-server.service

[Service]
Type=simple
User=youruser
WorkingDirectory=/opt/scipionweb/ScipionAPI-1.0.0
Environment=SCIPION_HOME=/opt/scipionweb/scipion_home
ExecStart=/home/youruser/miniconda3/envs/scipion4Web/bin/uvicorn app.backend.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080
Restart=always
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

Service dependencies

After= controls startup order. Wants= asks systemd to also start PostgreSQL and Redis when starting the API service.

docs.title: 4. Create the systemd Service for the Celery Worker
docs.text:
Create the service file:

/etc/systemd/system/scipion-celery.service

docs.title: Example scipion-celery.service
docs.text:
[Unit]
Description=ScipionAPI Celery Worker
After=network.target redis-server.service
Wants=redis-server.service

[Service]
Type=simple
User=youruser
WorkingDirectory=/opt/scipionweb/ScipionAPI-1.0.0
Environment=SCIPION_HOME=/opt/scipionweb/scipion_home
ExecStart=/home/youruser/miniconda3/envs/scipion4Web/bin/celery -A app.workers.task_queue worker --loglevel=info
Restart=always
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

Celery and API separation

Keeping the API and Celery worker in separate services makes restarts, monitoring, and troubleshooting much easier.

docs.title: 5. Reload systemd
docs.text:
Reload the systemd daemon after creating or modifying service files:

sudo systemctl daemon-reload

docs.title: 6. Enable Services on Boot
docs.text:
Enable both services so they start automatically after reboot:

sudo systemctl enable scipionapi
sudo systemctl enable scipion-celery

docs.title: 7. Start Services
docs.text:
Start both services:

sudo systemctl start scipionapi
sudo systemctl start scipion-celery

Start order

Start order between API and Celery is usually flexible, but Redis must be available before the worker can process tasks.

docs.title: 8. Check Status
docs.text:
Verify both services are active:

sudo systemctl status scipionapi
sudo systemctl status scipion-celery

For a quick summary:

systemctl is-active scipionapi
systemctl is-active scipion-celery

Expected output:

active
active

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
Follow logs in real time with journalctl:

journalctl -u scipionapi -f
journalctl -u scipion-celery -f

Show recent logs only

Useful filters:

  • journalctl -u scipionapi -n 100 --no-pager
  • journalctl -u scipion-celery -n 100 --no-pager

docs.title: Optional: nginx Reverse Proxy
docs.text:
Using nginx in front of ScipionAPI is recommended for:

  • HTTPS termination
  • Exposing ports 80 / 443
  • Reverse proxy headers
  • Load balancing (advanced setups)

docs.title: Minimal nginx proxy example
docs.text:
location / {
    proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
}

Integrated mode paths

If you use integrated mode (frontend served by the API) and custom API mount paths (for example /api), verify nginx forwards requests without breaking those routes.

docs.title: Run with a dedicated service user
docs.text: Instead of a personal account, consider a dedicated Linux user (for example scipion) to run the services.

docs.title: Restrict file permissions
docs.text:
Protect:

  • SCIPION_HOME/.env
  • Logs (if they may contain sensitive paths or errors)
  • Project data directories

docs.title: Keep backups before upgrades
docs.text:
Before upgrading ScipionAPI/ScipionWeb, backup:

  • PostgreSQL database
  • SCIPION_HOME/.env
  • Critical project data (if applicable)

docs.title: Test service restart behavior
docs.text:
After deployment, verify service restarts:

sudo systemctl restart scipionapi
sudo systemctl restart scipion-celery
sudo systemctl status scipionapi scipion-celery

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Service fails to start

Check:

  • WorkingDirectory exists
  • ExecStart points to the correct Conda environment binaries
  • SCIPION_HOME is correct
  • PostgreSQL and Redis are running
  • The installation works when started manually

ModuleNotFoundError in systemd logs

Usually caused by an incorrect WorkingDirectory or the wrong Python/Celery binary path in ExecStart.

Port 8080 already in use

Another process is already bound to the port. Stop the conflicting process or change the API port.

Celery starts but tasks do not run

Verify Redis connectivity, broker URL configuration, and check worker logs for import/configuration errors.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Using systemd provides:

  • Automatic restart on failure
  • Startup on boot
  • Centralized logging with journalctl
  • Better operational stability for production deployments

A minimal production setup typically includes:

  • scipionapi.service
  • scipion-celery.service
  • PostgreSQL
  • Redis
  • nginx (recommended for HTTPS/public exposure)
